# The FCC’s Spam Call Proposal Is Just a Data Collection Scheme

The Federal Communications Commission [wants to require telecommunications providers](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-27A1.pdf) to collect vast amounts of personal information from every person who wants a phone number in the name of combatting scam and spam calls. This plan will fail to combat the deluge of unwanted calls people in the United States receive every day while giving untrustworthy companies a gold mine of information that would harm everyday consumer’s privacy, access to communications, and ability to speak freely.

The requirement to provide ID and an address would [completely cut off the ability to have an anonymous phone line](https://www.404media.co/fcc-wants-to-kill-burner-phones-by-forcing-telecoms-to-get-all-customers-ids/) , which would mean many people in the most precarious situations imaginable: domestic violence and human trafficking survivors, unhoused people, and children without stable homes, would not be able to gain access to a crucial lifeline. EFF, along with ACLU, has [submitted comments advising the FCC to abandon this proposal entirely](https://eff.org/files/2026/06/25/2026.06.25_fcc_kyc_joint_comment.pdf).

**This Rule Will Not Decrease Spam Calls**

Requiring phone providers to collect consumers’ information will not appreciably decrease or eliminate unwanted calls. The FCC knows this because it [confesses in its own rulemaking](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-27A1.pdf) that “the most effective way to prevent unwanted calls from reaching American consumers is by ensuring they never enter the network.” Further, the Federal Trade Commission [found that](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2023/04/ftc-ramps-fight-close-door-illegal-robocalls-originating-overseas-scammers-imposters) “a significant proportion, if not the majority, of unwanted robocalls originate from overseas.” Collecting the personal information of everyone who wants to make a phone call will not put a dent in fraudulent calls.

What will address unwanted calls is the FCC’s [STIR/SHAKEN technical standards](https://www.fcc.gov/call-authentication) , which already exist. While STIR/SHAKEN is not perfect, it is actually a technical solution to the problem of spam calls. And where [less than 50% of American telecommunication providers have fully implemented the protocol](https://pirg.org/edfund/resources/robocall-mitigation-database-from-the-federal-communications-commission/) , the FCC should put its energy toward 100% compliance to reduce the scale of unwanted calls, instead of collecting consumer’s private information.

The FCC gives away the true reason for this proposal in their own comments: this is a move to shut down the very existence of anonymous phones, aka [burner phones](https://ssd.eff.org/glossary/burner-phone) . FCC says in their comments:

“Enhanced KYC information can assist law enforcement to more easily identify callers that use the network to perpetuate crimes by ensuring that voice providers have accurate and complete customer information. The KYC information gathered and verified would help ensure that law enforcement gets accurate information in response to subpoenas when investigating crimes. For example, can enhanced KYC rules assist law enforcement in investigating organized criminal groups that use the network to facilitate illegal activities? Can they be used to deter or detect trafficking operations that use communication networks to buy and sell illicit goods?”

Anonymous phones are not just used by people to break the law, they are also used by activists who wish to remain anonymous, privacy conscious consumers, people escaping domestic violence, people escaping human trafficking, journalists who need to reach out to confidential sources, and other people in desperate situations. Anonymous phone lines are a lifeline to many, one which this proposal would cut off without any alternative.

**Mass Data Collection Makes Us All Less Safe**

Mass data collection of individuals does not address unwanted calls, but it does

make us all less safe online. The telecommunications industry has proven time and again that they’re poor stewards of personal information. They’ve been at the center of several large-scale data breaches in recent years and their data practices leave much to be desired.

In 2024, AT&T disclosed two large data breaches. One in which [7.6 million existing account](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/personal-finance/att-data-breach-exposes-millions/) holders and more than 65 million former customers had their information leaked onto the dark web, and another in which [more than 100 million](https://www.reuters.com/technology/cybersecurity/att-says-data-around-109-mln-us-customer-accounts-illegally-downloaded-2024-07-12/) customer account call and text logs were downloaded. Another large provider, Comcast, suffered a data breach in 2023 where [nearly 36 million account holder’s](https://techcrunch.com/2023/12/19/comcast-xfinity-hackers-36-million-customers/) information was stolen, including the last four digits of their Social Security Number and date of birth.

In 2024, the nation’s CALEA infrastructure, which law enforcement uses to tap and trace calls, was [breached in the Salt Typhoon attacks](https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2024/10/salt-typhoon-hack-shows-theres-no-security-backdoor-thats-only-good-guys) . Experts maintain that U.S. communications networks [remain vulnerable](https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-salt-typhoon-ongoing-threat-cybertalks-2026/) , and even this administration acknowledges these attacks as an ongoing threat.

If telecoms can’t even protect the most sensitive communications infrastructure in the nation how can we expect that they will protect our identities?

In addition to their poor cybersecurity practice, these providers themselves abuse the information in their possession. In [Scott v AT&T,](https://www.eff.org/cases/geolocation-privacy) AT&T, among others, made consumer information available to hundreds of third parties without the consumer’s express consent. Though the case was dismissed because AT&T forces its consumers to sign arbitration agreements, it shows the complete lack of care for their consumers' privacy.

**A Lack of Anonymity Silences People**

Mass data collection of individuals just to have a phone number will also harm and silence people. Anonymity in calls provides people the safety they may require to organize themselves, speak freely, and seek services. Anonymous phone calls give people the courage to participate in politics, organize themselves, reach out to a suicide or sexual-assault hotline, an addiction-recovery sponsor, seek medical care, seek escape from a violent and coercive situation, and do much more. Without this anonymity, people may otherwise not do any of these things.

**It will prevent many from obtaining phone numbers at all.**

Not everyone has all the information the FCC wants to require. The FCC wants people’s physical addresses, defined so narrowly that it’s essentially a home address. Not everyone has a stable home address, so those individuals would be not able to get phone service.

FCC suggests that a government-issued identification should be required for any phone service. About 15 million adult U.S. citizens [do not have a driver’s license](https://cdce.umd.edu/sites/cdce.umd.edu/files/pubs/Voter%20ID%202023%20survey%20Key%20Results%20Jan%202024%20%281%29.pdf) , while about 2.6 million do not have any form of government-issued photo ID. Others don’t have access to their identifying documents, they may be controlled by an abusive spouse or parent, human trafficker, cult, or someone else from whom a secondary phone line could help a person escape. Estimates show another 21 million adult U.S. citizens do not have a non-expired driver’s license, and over 34.5 million adult citizens have neither a driver’s license nor a state ID card with their current name or address.

These numbers do not include non-U.S. citizens who do not have current government-issued identification, including undocumented immigrants who cannot obtain a state ID or driver’s license. Black American and Hispanic Americans are disproportionately less likely to have current drivers’ licenses, and Americans with disabilities and Americans with lower annual incomes are also less likely to have current driver’s licenses.

The FCC’s proposal will not decrease the amount of unwanted calls. All it will do is set up a data collection regime that harms everyday, law abiding Americans. This proposal makes us less secure online, strips away our right to anonymous speech in calls, and actively disconnects those Americans who are already at the margins. EFF recommends the FCC discard this proposal in its entirety.

The window for reply comments can still be filed until July 26th. Express comments, which are appropriate for most individuals, can be filed on the [FCC website](https://www.fcc.gov/ecfs/filings/express?proceeding%5Bname%5D=17-59) . See the suggested language below to help you get started.

# 聯邦通訊委員會的垃圾電話提案只是資料收集計畫

美國聯邦通訊委員會（FCC）[打算要求電信業者](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-27A1.pdf)從每位申請電話號碼的人身上蒐集大量個人資訊，以打擊詐騙與垃圾電話。然而，這項計畫不但無法有效減少美國人每天所收到的無聲騷擾電話，反而會將寶貴的消費者個資交給不可靠的公司，嚴重侵害公民隱私、通訊自由以及保障弱勢群體權益的能力。

要求提供身分證號碼與地址的規定[將徹底切斷匿名電話線路的可能](https://www.404media.co/fcc-wants-to-kill-burner-phones-by-forcing-telecoms-to-get-all-customers-ids/)，這對處於危險中的民眾來說是一場災難。例如：家暴與人口販運受害者、無家可歸者以及居住不穩定的兒童，將無法獲得一條關鍵的救命專線。電子隱私倡議（EFF）偕同美國公民自由聯盟（ACLU），已[向FCC提交意見書，強烈建議徹底撤回此提案](https://eff.org/files/2026/06/25/2026.06.25_fcc_kyc_joint_comment.pdf)。

**這項規定不會減少垃圾電話的數量**

要求電信業者蒐集消費者資料，並無法顯著降低或消除騷擾電話。FCC在其[自身的法規文件中](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-27A1.pdf)中坦承，「阻止無聲騷擾電話到達美國消費者的最有效方法，是確保這些電話永遠無法進入網路。」更何況，聯邦貿易委員會（FTC）[已經發現](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2023/04/ftc-ramps-fight-close-door-illegal-robocalls-originating-overseas-scammers-imposters)「絕大多數的無聲電話（未經授權的海外詐騙電話）都來自海外」。單純蒐集所有想撥打電話者的個資，並無法遏止詐騙電話。

什麼將解決騷擾電話的問題是 FCC 的 [STIR/SHAKEN 技術標準](https://www.fcc.gov/call-authentication)，這項技術標準已經存在。雖然 STIR/SHAKEN 並非完美，但它確實是一個針對阻礙電話的 spam 呼叫問題的技術解決方案。而目前僅有少於 50% 的美國電信業者已完全實施該協議 [FCC 電話授權資料庫](https://pirg.org/edfund/resources/robocall-mitigation-database-from-the-federal-communications-commission/)，FCC 應該將精力集中在實現 100% 合規上，以減少騷擾電話的規模，而非收集消費者的個人資訊。

FCC 在其自身評論中透露了此提案的真正原因：這是一項旨在關閉匿名手機（即 [burner phones](https://ssd.eff.org/glossary/burner-phone)）存在的舉措。FCC 說在評論中指出：

「強化 KYC（Know Your Customer）資訊可以協助執法單位更容易辨識利用該網路進行犯罪的通話者，確保電信業者擁有準確且完整的客戶資訊，當執法單位發出傳票調查犯罪時，能取得準確的資訊。例如，強化 KYC 規則是否能協助執法單位調查使用該網路促進非法活動的有組織犯罪集團？能否用於阻止或偵測利用通訊網路購買和販售非法商品的走私行動？」

匿名手機不僅是個人違法的工具，也是希望保持匿名的活動人士、注重隱私的消費者、逃離家庭暴力的受害者、逃離人口販運者、需要接觸機密來源的新聞工作者以及其他處於困境的人使用的工具。匿名電話線對許多人來說是一條生命線，而這項提案將在沒有替代方案的情況下切斷它。

**大規模資料收集使我們所有人都變得更不安全**

大規模收集個人資料並不能解決騷擾電話的問題，但卻會使我們所有人線上上都變得更不安全。電信業已多次證明其對個人資訊的監管能力不足。他們近年來一直是大型數據洩漏事件的核心，其資料處理方式令人擔憂。

2024 年，AT&T 揭露了兩起重大資料外洩事件。其中一起導致 [760 萬現有帳戶](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/personal-finance/att-data-breach-exposes-millions/)持有者的個資以及超過 6,500 萬前客戶的資訊外洩至暗網；另一起則是 [超過 1 億筆](https://www.reuters.com/technology/cybersecurity/att-says-data-around-109-mln-us-customer-accounts-illegally-downloaded-2024-07-12/)客戶通話與簡訊紀錄被非法下載。另一家大型營運商 Comcast 在 2023 年也遭遇資料外洩，導致 [近 3,600 萬帳戶持有者](https://techcrunch.com/2023/12/19/comcast-xfinity-hackers-36-million-customers/)的資訊被盜，包含其社會安全號碼後四位數與出生年月日。

2024 年，美國執法機關使用的 CALEA 基礎設施在「鹽颱風攻擊」中遭駭 [breached](https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2024/10/salt-typhoon-hack-shows-theres-no-security-backdoor-thats-only-good-guys)（[資料來源](https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-salt-typhoon-ongoing-threat-cybertalks-2026/)）。專家認為，即便此行政團隊已將這些攻擊視為持續威脅，美國的通訊網路仍處於高度脆弱狀態。如果連最敏感的國家級基礎設施都無法保護，我們能期待電信業者會妥善保護我們的個人身分嗎？

除了資安措施不足之外，這些營運商本身也濫用其持有的資訊。根據 [Scott v AT&T](https://www.eff.org/cases/geolocation-privacy)，AT&T 等公司在未經消費者同意的情況下，將消費者的個資提供給數百家第三方。雖然該案因 AT&T 強制使用者簽署仲裁協議而被駁回，但已充分顯示其對消費者隱私的漠視。

**匿名性缺失使人噤聲**

大量收集個人資料僅為取得電話號碼也會對人們造成傷害與沉默。通話的匿名性讓民眾在組織自己、自由發言以及尋求服務時能獲得所需的安全感。匿名的來電也能給予人們參與政治、組織活動、聯繫自殺或性侵害熱線、戒癮機構、尋求醫療照護、逃離暴力與脅迫情境等行動的勇氣。若沒有這層匿名性，許多人將無法進行這些事情。

**這可能導致許多人根本無法取得電話號碼。**

並非每個人都擁有聯邦通訊委員會（FCC）想要要求的全部資訊——他們希望獲取民眾的實體地址，這個定義極為狹窄，基本上就是家中的地址。由於並非所有人都有穩定的住所地址，因此這些人士將無法獲得電話服務。

FCC 建議任何電話服務都需要政府核發的身分證明。全美約有 1,500 萬成年美國公民沒有駕照（https://cdce.umd.edu/sites/cdce.umd.edu/files/pubs/Voter%20ID%202023%20survey%20Key%20Results%20Jan%202024%20%281%29.pdf），而約有 260 萬人沒有任何形式的政府核發的照片身分證。也有一些人不具備取得其識別文件的權限，可能受到虐待伴侶、家長、人口販子、邪教或其他人控制；若能透過額外的電話線路脫離困境，將有助於他們逃生。估計全美另有 2,100 萬成年美國公民沒有過期的駕照，而約有 3.45 億名成年美國公民既沒有駕照也沒有以當前姓名與地址的州級身分證。

這些數字不包括沒有持有現行政府核發身份文件的非美國公民，包括無法取得州級或駕照的無證移民；黑人與西班牙裔美國人的擁有駕駛執照機率比白人低很多，而有殘疾人士、年收入較低的成年人也更不容易擁有駕駛執照。

FCC 的提案並不會減少不想要的電話。它所做的只是建立一個資料收集制度，這會損害一般守法的美國民眾的日常體驗。此提案會使我們的網路安全性降低，剝奪我們在電話中進行匿名發言的權利，並且積極地將那些已經處於邊緣位置的人進一步隔絕。電子隱私倡議組織（EFF）強烈建議 FCC 完全放棄這項提案。

對於回覆評論的時間窗口仍然可以到 7 月 26 日前提交。適用多數人的即時評論可以在 [FCC 網站](https://www.fcc.gov/ecfs/filings/express?proceeding%5Bname%5D=17-59) 上提交。請參閱下方建議的文字以協助您開始撰寫。

# 聯邦通訊委員會的垃圾電話提案只是資料收集計畫

美國聯邦通訊委員會（FCC）[打算要求電信業者](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-27A1.pdf)從每位申請電話號碼的人身上蒐集大量個人資訊，以打擊詐騙與垃圾電話。然而，這項計畫不但無法有效減少美國人每天所收到的無聲騷擾電話，反而會將寶貴的消費者個資交給不可靠的公司，嚴重侵害公民隱私、通訊自由以及保障弱勢群體權益的能力。

要求提供身分證號碼與地址的規定[將徹底切斷匿名電話線路的可能](https://www.404media.co/fcc-wants-to-kill-burner-phones-by-forcing-telecoms-to-get-all-customers-ids/)，這對處於危險中的民眾來說是一場災難。例如：家暴與人口販運受害者、無家可歸者以及居住不穩定的兒童，將無法獲得一條關鍵的救命專線。電子隱私倡議（EFF）偕同美國公民自由聯盟（ACLU），已[向FCC提交意見書，強烈建議徹底撤回此提案](https://eff.org/files/2026/06/25/2026.06.25_fcc_kyc_joint_comment.pdf)。

**這項規定不會減少垃圾電話的數量**

要求電信業者蒐集消費者資料，並無法顯著降低或消除騷擾電話。FCC在其[自身的法規文件中](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-27A1.pdf)中坦承，「阻止無聲騷擾電話到達美國消費者的最有效方法，是確保這些電話永遠無法進入網路。」更何況，聯邦貿易委員會（FTC）[已經發現](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2023/04/ftc-ramps-fight-close-door-illegal-robocalls-originating-overseas-scammers-imposters)「絕大多數的無聲電話（未經授權的海外詐騙電話）都來自海外」。單純蒐集所有想撥打電話者的個資，並無法遏止詐騙電話。

什麼將解決騷擾電話的問題是 FCC 的 [STIR/SHAKEN 技術標準](https://www.fcc.gov/call-authentication)，這項技術標準已經存在。雖然 STIR/SHAKEN 並非完美，但它確實是一個針對阻礙電話的 spam 呼叫問題的技術解決方案。而目前僅有少於 50% 的美國電信業者已完全實施該協議 [FCC 電話授權資料庫](https://pirg.org/edfund/resources/robocall-mitigation-database-from-the-federal-communications-commission/)，FCC 應該將精力集中在實現 100% 合規上，以減少騷擾電話的規模，而非收集消費者的個人資訊。

FCC 在其自身評論中透露了此提案的真正原因：這是一項旨在關閉匿名手機（即 [burner phones](https://ssd.eff.org/glossary/burner-phone)）存在的舉措。FCC 說在評論中指出：

「強化 KYC（Know Your Customer）資訊可以協助執法單位更容易辨識利用該網路進行犯罪的通話者，確保電信業者擁有準確且完整的客戶資訊，當執法單位發出傳票調查犯罪時，能取得準確的資訊。例如，強化 KYC 規則是否能協助執法單位調查使用該網路促進非法活動的有組織犯罪集團？能否用於阻止或偵測利用通訊網路購買和販售非法商品的走私行動？」

匿名手機不僅是個人違法的工具，也是希望保持匿名的活動人士、注重隱私的消費者、逃離家庭暴力的受害者、逃離人口販運者、需要接觸機密來源的新聞工作者以及其他處於困境的人使用的工具。匿名電話線對許多人來說是一條生命線，而這項提案將在沒有替代方案的情況下切斷它。

**大規模資料收集使我們所有人都變得更不安全**

大規模收集個人資料並不能解決騷擾電話的問題，但卻會使我們所有人線上上都變得更不安全。電信業已多次證明其對個人資訊的監管能力不足。他們近年來一直是大型數據洩漏事件的核心，其資料處理方式令人擔憂。

2024 年，AT&T 揭露了兩起重大資料外洩事件。其中一起導致 [760 萬現有帳戶](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/personal-finance/att-data-breach-exposes-millions/)持有者的個資以及超過 6,500 萬前客戶的資訊外洩至暗網；另一起則是 [超過 1 億筆](https://www.reuters.com/technology/cybersecurity/att-says-data-around-109-mln-us-customer-accounts-illegally-downloaded-2024-07-12/)客戶通話與簡訊紀錄被非法下載。另一家大型營運商 Comcast 在 2023 年也遭遇資料外洩，導致 [近 3,600 萬帳戶持有者](https://techcrunch.com/2023/12/19/comcast-xfinity-hackers-36-million-customers/)的資訊被盜，包含其社會安全號碼後四位數與出生年月日。

2024 年，美國執法機關使用的 CALEA 基礎設施在「鹽颱風攻擊」中遭駭 [breached](https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2024/10/salt-typhoon-hack-shows-theres-no-security-backdoor-thats-only-good-guys)（[資料來源](https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-salt-typhoon-ongoing-threat-cybertalks-2026/)）。專家認為，即便此行政團隊已將這些攻擊視為持續威脅，美國的通訊網路仍處於高度脆弱狀態。如果連最敏感的國家級基礎設施都無法保護，我們能期待電信業者會妥善保護我們的個人身分嗎？

除了資安措施不足之外，這些營運商本身也濫用其持有的資訊。根據 [Scott v AT&T](https://www.eff.org/cases/geolocation-privacy)，AT&T 等公司在未經消費者同意的情況下，將消費者的個資提供給數百家第三方。雖然該案因 AT&T 強制使用者簽署仲裁協議而被駁回，但已充分顯示其對消費者隱私的漠視。

**匿名性缺失使人噤聲**

大量收集個人資料僅為取得電話號碼也會對人們造成傷害與沉默。通話的匿名性讓民眾在組織自己、自由發言以及尋求服務時能獲得所需的安全感。匿名的來電也能給予人們參與政治、組織活動、聯繫自殺或性侵害熱線、戒癮機構、尋求醫療照護、逃離暴力與脅迫情境等行動的勇氣。若沒有這層匿名性，許多人將無法進行這些事情。

**這可能導致許多人根本無法取得電話號碼。**

並非每個人都擁有聯邦通訊委員會（FCC）想要要求的全部資訊——他們希望獲取民眾的實體地址，這個定義極為狹窄，基本上就是家中的地址。由於並非所有人都有穩定的住所地址，因此這些人士將無法獲得電話服務。

FCC 建議任何電話服務都需要政府核發的身分證明。全美約有 1,500 萬成年美國公民沒有駕照（https://cdce.umd.edu/sites/cdce.umd.edu/files/pubs/Voter%20ID%202023%20survey%20Key%20Results%20Jan%202024%20%281%29.pdf），而約有 260 萬人沒有任何形式的政府核發的照片身分證。也有一些人不具備取得其識別文件的權限，可能受到虐待伴侶、家長、人口販子、邪教或其他人控制；若能透過額外的電話線路脫離困境，將有助於他們逃生。估計全美另有 2,100 萬成年美國公民沒有過期的駕照，而約有 3.45 億名成年美國公民既沒有駕照也沒有以當前姓名與地址的州級身分證。

這些數字不包括沒有持有現行政府核發身份文件的非美國公民，包括無法取得州級或駕照的無證移民；黑人與西班牙裔美國人的擁有駕駛執照機率比白人低很多，而有殘疾人士、年收入較低的成年人也更不容易擁有駕駛執照。

FCC 的提案並不會減少不想要的電話。它所做的只是建立一個資料收集制度，這會損害一般守法的美國民眾的日常體驗。此提案會使我們的網路安全性降低，剝奪我們在電話中進行匿名發言的權利，並且積極地將那些已經處於邊緣位置的人進一步隔絕。電子隱私倡議組織（EFF）強烈建議 FCC 完全放棄這項提案。
